title: A Kite Festival on a Spring Afternoon
subtheme: A Kite Festival on a Spring Afternoon
description: Colorful frames and long lines fill a breezy field at a spring celebration.
cardDescription: Colorful frames and long lines fill a breezy field at a spring celebration.
focus: The setting is a Kite Festival on a Spring Afternoon. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Light framed toy flown at the end of a line
Rear extension of an animal's body
Hue, such as red or blue
Spool storing film or fishing line

answerNotes.WIND: Wind has two pronunciations and meanings: moving air, or turning something around a center. A yarn ball or clock uses the turning action.
answerNotes.SKY: Sky describes the overhead view from the ground. Clouds, the Sun, the Moon, and stars can all appear in that view.
answerNotes.STRING: String is a thin cord used for tying or flying a kite. A kite's string connects the flying frame to the person holding it.
answerNotes.TAIL: Tail can name the rear part of an animal or a trailing end of ribbon or a kite. The word describes different things with a similar extending position.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.
answerNotes.FLAG: A flag can be a cloth symbol or a small signaling marker. A mailbox flag shows a postal signal rather than identifying a country.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.REEL: A reel stores a long flexible strip or line. A fishing reel takes up line, while a film reel holds a strip of images.

words: Small shallow pool of rainwater on the ground
To scatter water by striking or stepping into it
Paved pedestrian path beside a residential street
White or gray mass in the sky
Image seen in a mirror or still water

answerNotes.RAIN: Rain is liquid water falling from clouds. Snow and hail reach the ground in solid forms instead.
answerNotes.BOOT: A boot rises above the ankle. Its sole can leave a tread pattern in mud or snow.
answerNotes.CLOUD: Clouds contain tiny water droplets, ice crystals, or both. Their gray appearance does not mean the water itself is gray.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.STEP: Step can name an action or one level of a stairway. In a stepping-stone clue, it concerns placing a foot on the next surface.
answerNotes.COAT: A coat is an outer garment. Its lining is inside, while the collar and pockets are visible features outside.

A familiar swimming bird that may quack
Soft, fluffy feathers that help keep a bird warm
Move through water using webbed feet
Go behind someone along the same path
Rest on top of water rather than sink
Part a bird spreads to fly

answerNotes.YELLOW: Yellow is a color name rather than a material. The movie's yellow brick road combines a color with a building block.
answerNotes.POND: A pond is a small body of still water. A creek or brook flows along a channel instead.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.SWIM: Swimming uses the body to move through water. Floating means remaining supported at the surface without necessarily traveling.
answerNotes.FOOT: A foot is a body part and also a unit of length. A shoe clue points to the body meaning rather than twelve inches.
answerNotes.MOTHER: Mother names a female parent. In a story scene, the surrounding names help show which family relationship is being described.
answerNotes.FAMILY: Family can include several generations and relatives by marriage. A family tree shows relationships rather than everyone's physical appearance.
answerNotes.WING: Wings help birds, many insects, and airplanes fly, but their structures differ. The model-airplane scene uses a fixed surface rather than feathers.

title: A First Picnic After Winter
description: Pack an outdoor meal for the first mild days after winter.
cardDescription: Pack an outdoor meal for the first mild days after winter.
focus: The setting is a First Picnic After Winter. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Outdoor meal packed in a basket
Large soft covering used for warmth
Food made with filling between pieces of bread
Round tree fruit with a core
Cloth or paper square used at a meal
Public green space where people may walk dogs

answerNotes.SPRING: Spring is the season between winter and summer. Weather and the exact timing of flowers vary by U.S. region.
answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.BASKET: A basket is made by weaving flexible material. Its open structure and carrying handle make it useful for collecting garden produce.
answerNotes.SANDWICH: A sandwich places a filling between pieces of bread. An open-faced version uses just one supporting slice.
answerNotes.JUICE: Juice is liquid released from fruit or vegetables. Pulp is the soft plant material that may remain mixed into it.
answerNotes.APPLE: An apple has a peel, flesh, and a seed-bearing core. Cider is made by pressing apples for their juice.
answerNotes.GRASS: Grass commonly covers lawns and meadows. A pasture is land where animals graze on grass and other low plants.
answerNotes.SUN: The Sun is a star. Its closeness makes it look much larger and brighter than the points of light seen at night.
answerNotes.BENCH: A bench normally seats more than one person. It can be used in a park, entryway, or bus shelter without changing that basic meaning.
answerNotes.BLOOM: Bloom can mean an open flower or the act of flowering. In a flower clue, it does not mean a leafy bud that has not opened.

answerNotes.GLOVE: A glove has separate spaces for the fingers. A mitten groups the fingers together and has a separate space for the thumb.
answerNotes.BASEBALL: Baseball uses a bat, ball, and gloves. Its field and equipment clues concern the sport rather than professional-player trivia.
answerNotes.MITT: A mitt is a catching glove with joined finger sections. It is related to but not identical with an ordinary five-finger glove.
answerNotes.LACE: A shoelace threads through openings to fasten a shoe. Lace can also name decorative openwork fabric, a different sense.
answerNotes.BALL: A ball is usually round in games such as baseball. American football uses a different, elongated shape.
answerNotes.FIELD: A field can be open farmland or a sports playing area. The Thanksgiving game scene uses the sports meaning.
answerNotes.SPRING: Spring is the season between winter and summer. Weather and the exact timing of flowers vary by U.S. region.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.
